rules.road_width: OSM width, else by class (ROAD_WIDTH in tools/scene_builder/ground.py).
rules.water: OSM water polygons that close inside the data box; the river level is y = 0 (terrain cells under 0.8 m are river in HRDEM here).
rules.surface_class: `sf` is the OSM `surface` word mapped to the format's surface class (SURFACE_WORDS in tools/scene_builder/ground.py), else the style pack's street.surface for the road class, else asphalt.
rules.sidewalks: `sw`: none where tagged sidewalk=no|none|separate or where a mapped footway=sidewalk way runs within 6 m along most of the road; the tagged side where tagged; else both for the classes in the style pack's street.sidewalk.on, else none.
rules.sidewalk_ways: A way mapped as footway=sidewalk is itself a raised sidewalk (`sw` "self"), 1.6 m wide unless tagged.
rules.steps: `sc` step_count where tagged, else round(rise / 0.17) and at least 2; `hr` from handrail*= tags (0 none, 1 both sides, 2 centre).
rules.markings: `mk` = 1 (centre line) on primary, secondary and tertiary roads with an asphalt surface; `lit` from lit=yes.
rules.crossings: highway=crossing nodes snapped to the nearest road vertex or segment within 1.5 m, [x, z, bearing, road width]; others dropped.
rules.bare_ground: Ground no road, area, building or water covers, on 5 m cells: slope over 0.6 (rise over run, terrain model) is rock, 0.25 to 0.6 outside any green is a grassy bank; merged into rectangles in `areas` with k 'bare'.
rules.crossing_ways: A footway=crossing way takes the surface class of the street it crosses, so the street stays one surface; the `crossings` layer draws the zebra.
rules.wall_height: A wall's thickness, material, free height and parapet come from the style pack (`walls`); OSM `height` and `width` win. Where the ground differs by more than 1.5 m between 1.5 m either side of the wall along 60 % of a run, the wall holds ground back: it is written with `hp` (its top stands that far above the higher ground) and no `h`; a way is cut into such runs at the vertices where this changes, no run under 10 m. Fences, handrails and guard rails are drawn as rails and never hold ground.
rules.gates: A building passage: a road (not steps) tagged tunnel=building_passage, or any road under a building tagged historic=city_gate, takes its width (at least 3 m, at most the footprint's width across the way minus 2 × 1.2 m of pier) through the footprint, 0.5 m beyond it at each end, clear height the lower of 0.7 × the eave and the width + 1 m. The building is then drawn flat roofed with no shopfront.
rules.terraces: Terrace rules of the place file: the matched pedestrian area is drawn as a deck of boards (`terraces`, board width and direction from the rule), its edges where the ground outside is lower than inside by the rule's drop within 4 m carry a balustrade (written as wall records with `rail`; 22 runs) and lamps stand on that line every rule spacing m.
rules.street_lamps: Street lamps by rule (source 2): every 24 m along each road of the style pack's street.lamps `on` classes (not tunnels, bridges or steps), 0.6 m behind the kerb line, alternating sides when `stagger`; a lamp inside a building footprint (or within 0.4 m of it) moves to the other side once; none within 9.6 m of another lamp. 409 placed, dropped: 56 inside a building, 29 too close to another lamp, 85 outside the extent.
rules.place_props: Props placed by the place file's `props` (source 3): 1 item(s) at the given lat/lon, the bearing given in degrees true turned to grid by the scene's convergence, whole-metre-tenths position; `on: water` sets the item's own height (a 7th field) to the water level and fails the build where the point is neither inside a water polygon nor on terrain at or under the water level (+0.05 m).
rules.props: Props: OSM nodes whose key=value is in the style pack's `props` (and shelters with a round footprint, as open pavilions) become prop items (source 0); direction from the `direction` tag, benches face the nearest terrace balustrade within 14 m; terrace lamps (source 1) stand on the rail line every rule spacing, street lamps (source 2) along the roads, the place file's own props are source 3. 436 items are placed by rule or by the place file.
rules.trees: Trees: 345 mapped natural=tree nodes (source 0; kind and form from the style's trees.genus and the leaf_type tag, height and crown from the tags, else the measured canopy dsm - dtm where no building is within 4 m, else the style's size table). By rule, each seeded and style-driven (style trees.fill): 24 along tree_row ways every 8 m (source 1); 200 in woods, forest and scrub at 1.2 (scrub 0.5) per 100 m2 on a jittered grid (source 2); 275 in parks, gardens, cemeteries and grass at 0.35 per 100 m2, 2.5 m from buildings and ways (source 3); 300 on unbuilt, unpaved ground steeper than 0.45 at 0.8 per 100 m2, at 0.7 of the size (source 4); 43 street trees every 14 m, 0.8 m behind the kerb, only where the sidewalk is 2.2 m wide or a grass verge is, not within 3 m of a lamp, 1.2 m of a building or a junction mouth (source 5). Never in a building, on a road or sidewalk, in water or on a mapped square; at least 1.8 m between trees. Height and crown vary by ±15 % (seeded). Cap 4000: not reached. Dropped by rule: parks: 22 at a building, 1 at a prop, 3 in water, 27 on a paved square, 174 on a road or sidewalk, 244 outside the extent, 4 too close to a tree; rows: 16 outside the extent; slope: 10 at a building, 11 at a wall, 5 on a road or sidewalk, 9 too close to a tree; street: 1 at a building, 33 at a junction mouth or another way, 6 near a lamp, 1396 no wide sidewalk or verge, 18 outside the extent, 1 too close to a tree; woods: 6 at a building, 1 at a wall, 2 on a road or sidewalk, 100 outside the extent, 1 too close to a tree.
rules.street_parking: Parked vehicles by rule (source 4, static): along the style pack's street.parking `on` classes at least 6.5 m wide (not tunnels or bridges), on one side only (the left of travel for an even way id, else the right), parallel to the kerb with the car's side 0.25 m off the kerb line, in 6 m slots each filled with chance 0.22; never within 8 m of a junction, crossing, road end, steps, tunnel or bridge, nor where less than 3 m of carriageway would be left beside the car; heading along the road within 2 degrees. Bicycles (chance 0.08 per 10 m) on sidewalks 1.8 m wide or more, against the wall. 126 vehicles and 0 bicycles placed from 300 filled slots; dropped: 9 a bend, 13 a building, wall, tree or other street in the way, 96 near a junction, a crossing or a road end, 24 outside the extent, 32 too steep.
rules.street_people: Bystanders by rule (source 5, static, scenery: not threats, never scored): 0.6 groups per 100 m of sidewalk and 2 per 1 000 m2 of pedestrian area (squares, pedestrian streets), a group of 1 to 3 people 0.6 to 0.9 m apart facing each other (singles along the street), at least 0.5 m from walls, kerbs and buildings, never on a carriageway, 1.6 m between groups. 168 people in 104 groups placed (144 sidewalk and 68 square candidates); dropped: 5 against another prop or vehicle, 8 in or within 0.5 m of a building, 44 on or within 0.5 m of a carriageway, 3 on steps, 46 outside the extent, 2 within 0.5 m of a wall.
rules.landmarks: Place landmark rules (places/<id>.json `landmarks`): chateau-frontenac: 4 part(s) fill the outline's uncovered area (4044 m²), measured like any part | chateau-frontenac: 6 round corner turrets (radius 3.0 m, conical roof 8.5 m) are an estimate: the map has none; they stand on the outer corners of the parts between [70, 110] degrees | chateau-frontenac: Heights, roof shapes and roof colour of the building:part ways are OpenStreetMap (ODbL) and the HRDEM surface model (OGL-Canada). Brick walls with stone dressing, verdigris copper roofs and corner turrets are the look noted in docs/plans/QUEBEC-LOOK.md section 2 (Chateau, gates, churches); that note is the only source for the look. The part of the outline no mapped part covers is filled with parts measured the same way. The round corner turrets (6.0 m across, conical roof 8.5 m, 2.5 m above the eave of the part they stand on) are an estimate: the map has none.
rules.building_height: Height `h` is the top of the roof above `g`, the lowest ground at the footprint. In order: OSM height (`hs` tag); the measured height (`hs` measured): the 95th percentile of the HRDEM surface model minus `g` over a 1 m lattice inside the footprint, 1 m clear of its edges (on a narrow roof the fitted roof slope is carried to the footprint's inradius when that is higher), kept when it lies between 3 and 150 m; building:levels × 3.1 m (levels); by kind: church/cathedral/chapel 18 m, hotel/civic/school/university/government/public 16 m, garage/shed/hut/roof/kiosk 3 m, footprint over 1500 m² 15 m, under 40 m² 4 m, otherwise 10.5 m (rule).
rules.roof: OSM roof:shape where tagged; otherwise the style pack picks `rs` by weight, seeded by the building id.
rules.roof_shape: Roof shape: a tagged roof:shape wins; else the first rule of the style pack that matches the building kind, use, area, storeys, attached walls and measured roof pitch (flat, low or steep, from the rise of the roof against the half width of the footprint) picks by weight. Under 4 vertices or 20 m²: flat. A footprint with a courtyard: flat, mansard or hipped.
rules.ridge_direction: `rd` is a bearing 0-179 from grid north: roof:direction (+90°: OSM gives the way the roof faces) or roof:orientation where tagged; else, for a measured gabled, gambrel or skillion roof, the axis of the oriented footprint along which the roof stays level, when height and distance from that axis correlate below -0.3; otherwise 255 (along the longest side).
rules.roof_height: `rh` is the roof above the eave: roof:height where tagged; else the measured rise: the ridge minus the eave, the eave being a straight line fitted to the surface height against the distance to the nearest wall (samples 1 to 4 m in, outliers dropped) and read at the wall, at least 2.2 m above ground and at most 0.5 m above the 20th percentile of the roof; clamped to 0.8 m and 0.9 h - 2.4 m; a roof whose fit rises less than 0.08 m per m and whose rise is under 0.8 m is flat (0). Mansard 3.2 m when not measured, at most 4.2 m; else half the footprint width × tan of the style's pitch, between 1.2 m and 0.45 h.
rules.levels: `lv` is building:levels where tagged, else the eave height divided by the style's storey height (3.1 m), at least 1.
rules.facade: `fa` and `rmt`: building:material and roof:material where tagged (a green roof:colour means copper); else the style pack's weighted pick. `pal` and `rp` are seeded picks within the style's colour list; the town is the same on every build.
rules.use: `use`: from the building kind, or retail/food/hotel/museum points of interest inside the footprint or within 3 m of it (commercial).
rules.blind_edges: `blind` lists the edges of a footprint with no openings: at least two of the points at a quarter, half and three quarters of the edge, 0.6 m outwards, lie inside another building; edges under 1.2 m.
rules.front_edges: `front` lists the edges that face a street: not blind, 2.5 m or more, within half a road width + 6 m of a road (not service, steps, path, corridor or tunnel) with the outward normal pointing at it. `gf` is 1 for a commercial building with a front edge, 2 for garages.
rules.building_id: `id`: FNV-1a 32 of "<osm type>/<osm id>/<ring index>", +1 on a clash, never 0.
rules.simplify: Rings and lines simplified to 0.25 m (Douglas-Peucker), coordinates rounded to 0.1 m.

terrain.encoding: base64 uint16 little-endian, rows north to south
